Cutting out Episode 1 not only saves you from Jar Jar's antics and midichlorians, but it won't narratively disrupt the pace of the series. As RedLetterMedia puts it in their infamous Plinkett Review of The Phantom Menace there's basically no protagonist nor any relatable character in Episode I. Furthermore, there's a lack of investment in the conflict because even the Jedi aren't invested in the conflict. For all the flaws in Episode 2 and 3, they at least have clear cut protagonist with a clear cut conflict (Anakin wishes the protect Padme even if it compromises him as a Jedi) that aid the backstory of Darth Vader for Episode 6.

Episode 1 is unnecessary in the context of the series, especially when viewing it in Machete Order, which is meant to show parallel the stories of Luke and Anakin.

Machete order best order! No Jar Jar, no Qui Gon, no midichlorians, no Darth Maul (a "storyline" that begins and ends without any real explanation), just no Phantom. It is really cool to watch in this order because you watch A New Hope and Empire, then take a big flashback with AOTC and ROTS. The way the end of Empire leaves you hanging, this is really good. Yes AOTC and ROTS aren't good and are pretty boring, but by watching AOTC and ROTS right after Empire, you are essentially seeing the Vader reveal and then taking a huge flashback to see his origin. Then right back into ROTJ for the conclusion.

tl;dr 4,5,2,3,6

Best viewing order is the Machete Order. 4, 5, 1 (optional), 2, 3, 6.

This gives you the introduction to the story that Lucas intended and preserves the reveal in 5, as well. A lot of people would continue on to 6 from here and finish with 1, 2, and 3, but then you're left with a "bad" ending. Watching the prequels as a flashback that expands on Anakin's fall to the dark side is best to do right after the reveal. "Holy shit, Vader's his dad? Whaaaaat? Oh, the prequels explain." And then you end with the "good" ending of 6.
